newsitem.title: USA: World Bank approves $800 mln loan to Russia.
newsitem.headline: World Bank approves $800 mln loan to Russia.

text.p: The World Bank said on Wednesday its board had approved an $800 million loan to back Russia's social reforms, the third biggest loan in the history of the institution.
The loan, to help Russia develop an adequate system to protect those losing out from economic reforms, is part of a $1.7 billion loan package announced earlier this month.

World Bank President James Wolfensohn has said the bank could lend Russia $10 billion over the next three years, mainly in projects designed to help ease the painful social consequences of economic reform.
This could eventually make the World Bank a bigger lender to Russia than the International Monetary Fund, which is backing Mosow's economic reform program with a $10 billion three-year loan.
Several World Bank loans were approved earlier this month, including a $600 million credit for structural reform.
